> I watched the tapestry for some time, and presently I became aware that it was not hanging quietly, but was gently undulating, as though it were breathing. Then it began to undulate more vigorously, and I noticed that the design was curling in a most peculiar manner, as though it were trying to detach itself from the rest of the tapestry. I watched, fascinated, as the curling became more and more pronounced, until at last a separate piece detached itself and came sliding down the tapestry like a tongue. It hung there for a moment, a good two feet long and writhing gently, then it shot out across the chancel and wrapped itself round my neck. I tried to tear it away, but I could not move; I was paralyzed with fear. I looked up and saw that the tapestry was undulating more violently than ever, and that more tongues were working themselves loose. One by one they shot out across the chancel and began to coil themselves round me, round my arms and legs and body, and gradually to pull me in towards the tapestry. I struggled, but I could not free myself; I was held as though in a vise. I looked up again and saw that the whole tapestry was coming alive. It was no longer a tapestry, but a monstrous, writhing creature, and I was being dragged remorselessly into its gaping, seething mouth. I could feel its hot breath on my face, and I knew that in a moment I would be swallowed up and devoured.

I looked round and saw that the creature had fallen back upon the tapestry and was lying there, a great, shapeless, twitching mass, its tongues still writhing and lashing about. I turned and ran up the chancel towards the altar, and as I did so I heard the sound of voices. I looked round and saw that the place was full of people, staring up at me in terror.
